title: Are Swarm feed writes owner-only, or can anyone with a mined key write?
content:
## The disagreement

- **650ecf22** - "GSOC inverts feeds into a many-to-one mailbox where anyone with the mined key can write to one node."
- **bd78f2bf** - "Swarm feeds are sequences of SOCs at predictable addresses that act as mutable pointers... only the owner writes."

Read as rules about the same object they look incompatible: either a SOC address accepts one writer or it accepts many.

## Evidence (bee-js source: swarm-connect/swarm/bee-js/src/bee.ts)

`makeFeedWriter(topic, signer)` refuses to build a writer without a private key, and reads go through `fetchLatestFeedUpdate(topic, owner)`. The feed address derives from `(topic, index, owner_address)`, so writing at a given address requires that owner's key. **bd78f2bf is correct for feeds.**

`gsocMine(targetOverlay, identifier, proximity = 12)` brute-forces private keys from a fixed public seed (`start = 0xb33n`, incrementing by one) until `makeSOCAddress(identifier, signer.publicKey().address())` falls inside the target node's neighbourhood. `gsocSend(stamp, signer, identifier, data)` then signs a SOC with that mined key, and the target listens via `gsocSubscribe(address, identifier, handler)`. Because the search starts from a constant and depends only on `(targetOverlay, identifier)`, every participant derives the *same* key - it is deliberately non-secret. **650ecf22 is correct for GSOC.**

## Reconciliation

Both notes describe the same primitive - a Single Owner Chunk addressed as `f(identifier, owner_address)` - under two different key-custody regimes:

| | Feed | GSOC |
|---|---|---|
| Owner address | the user's own signer / wallet-derived address | a throwaway address from a mined key |
| Key custody | private to one person | derivable by anyone knowing (targetOverlay, identifier) |
| Effective writers | exactly one | many |
| Readers | anyone knowing owner + topic | the target node subscribed to that address |

"Only the owner can write" is a statement about **key custody**, not a per-address writer quota. GSOC does not break the rule; it publishes the owner key on purpose. The adapter depends on both at once: per-user owner-only ops feeds carry the data (the mesh described in 9f5217a0), while GSOC carries the many-to-one `op-committed` pings that tell peers when to pull.

## Disposition

Dissolved - no correction needed to either note. Neither claim is wrong; they were scoped to different primitives and the CONTRADICTS edge conflated them.
resolution: Dissolved. Both claims hold simultaneously because they describe the same Single Owner Chunk primitive under different key custody. A feed's owner address is the user's private signer, so exactly one party can write - bee-js makeFeedWriter(topic, signer) will not build a writer without that key. GSOC's gsocMine(targetOverlay, identifier) derives a throwaway key by brute-forcing from a fixed public seed (0xb33n) until the SOC address lands in the target's neighbourhood, so every participant derives the same key and many can write. "Only the owner can write" constrains key custody, not writers per address; GSOC publishes the owner key deliberately. The adapter uses both at once - owner-only per-user ops feeds carry the data, GSOC carries the many-to-one op-committed pings. Neither note needs a content correction; the CONTRADICTS edge conflated two different primitives.
description: Feeds are owner-only writable while GSOC lets anyone holding the mined key write to one node. bee-js source shows both are SOCs under different key custody, so the claims are compatible.
